subject: The farm is yours
body:
My dear sprout,

If you're reading this, you've found the old place. I'm sorry about the weeds. My knees gave out long before the soil did.

The farm is yours now. Bramblewick could use a farmer again: the mill is quiet, the market's shuttered, and the road is half buried in rocks. Start small. A few radishes never hurt anyone.

Goldie at the store will look in on you. Tell her I said she still owes me a pie.

With love and dirt under my nails,
Tobias

subject: About that gate
body:
Hello neighbour,

Goldie tells me Tobias's gate finally fell off its hinges. I can rebuild it, and open up the field behind it while I'm at it.

Bring me 4 wood, 3 stone and 60 coins. Branches and rocks around your farm will do nicely.

Bruno

subject: Your gate is up!
body:
Morning!

Worked through the night. The new gate swings like a dream, and the back field is yours to clear. Mind the rocks.

Bruno

P.S. Goldie says she'll pay well for anything you grow out there.

subject: About old Rufus
body:
Hello dear,

You've done wonders with that farm. Now I need a favour.

Rufus ran the mill until the wheel jammed. He's been sulking up there ever since. He'll say he doesn't want help. He does.

He'll be by your gate. Be patient with him.

Goldie

subject: The wheel turns
body:
Farmer,

I heard it this morning before I even opened my eyes. That creak. That splash. Twenty years I've waited for that sound.

The mill is yours to use. Bring wheat, take flour. No charge. Don't make it weird.

Rufus

subject: I heard about the mill
body:
My dear sprout,

News travels up the valley faster than the river. The mill is turning again! Rufus wrote to me himself, and he hasn't written to anyone since 1998.

Next, the market square. Bramblewick used to fill it every Saturday. Someone there still bakes the best bread in the valley, if only she had the flour.

Proud of you,
Tobias

subject: THE MARKET IS OPEN
body:
Dear farmer,

I walked through the square at sunrise and every stall was standing. There's bunting! Bruno even painted my stall pink. I didn't ask for pink. I love the pink.

Opening day is today. I have absolutely nothing ready. Please come by.

Pip

P.S. Sorry about the capital letters in the subject.

subject: About my seed collection
body:
My dear sprout,

A market again! Pip wrote to me in three colours of ink.

Ziggy tells me Dr. Hazel Quill is coming to Bramblewick. She and I traded seeds for forty years, and I left her my whole collection: every crop I ever grew, written down in a battered old almanac.

Help her finish it. She'll pretend she doesn't need help. She does.

With love,
Tobias
